Few inventions in human history have reshaped civilization as profoundly as the printing press. The ability to reproduce text mechanically—rapidly, cheaply, and in quantity—transformed religion, politics, science, education, and culture across the globe. What follows is a detailed account of the printing press's history, from its distant precursors in Asia through its refinement in Europe, its spread across the world, its industrial evolution, and its eventual displacement by digital technologies. The story of the printing press is, in many ways, the story of how knowledge became a public good rather than a guarded treasure.

Long before Johannes Gutenberg assembled his movable-type press in the fifteenth century, societies in East Asia had already developed sophisticated printing technologies. Few inventions in human history have reshaped civilization as profoundly as the printing press. The ability to reproduce text mechanically—rapidly, cheaply, and in quantity—transformed religion, politics, science, education, and commerce across the globe.
